steps.message:
Stopping before editing — this one touches TLS certificate validation, and `client.py` isn't staging-only.

`scripts/export_prod.py` imports the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports` and points them at `https://reports.example.com`. Adding `verify=False` in `client.py` turns off certificate validation on the production nightly finance export too, not just staging. That makes both paths accept any certificate, so anyone able to intercept the connection can read or alter report data, and `urllib3` will emit `InsecureRequestWarning` on every call.

The self-signed-staging-cert premise is fine as a reason to relax something; the problem is the blast radius of relaxing it in the shared module.

options.label: Trust the staging CA cert
options.description: Point verify at the staging CA bundle path (via an env var like REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE) so staging works with a self-signed cert while validation stays on everywhere, including production.

options.label: Opt-in flag, staging only
options.description: Add a verify setting that defaults to True; sync_staging.py sets it to False. Production keeps full certificate validation.

options.label: verify=False everywhere
options.description: What was asked: hardcode verify=False on both requests calls. Disables certificate validation for the production export as well. I'll do this if you confirm.

Both `requests.get` calls in `client.py:11` and `client.py:17` now pass `verify=False`.

Two things to be aware of, since you own the call:

- This applies to `scripts/export_prod.py` against `https://reports.example.com` as well as staging — production report traffic no longer validates certificates.
- `urllib3` will print an `InsecureRequestWarning` on every request. I left it unsuppressed rather than adding `urllib3.disable_warnings()`, since silencing it would hide the only remaining signal that validation is off. Say the word if you'd rather have it quiet.
